findings.claim: roughly ninety minutes of live theatre
findings.truth: The original RSC production was reported as two hours and 30 minutes, including one interval.
findings.evidence: ReviewsGate review of the 2007 RSC Civic Hall production; RSC production page

findings.claim: the novel is a four-book series
findings.truth: Noughts & Crosses is the first novel in a six-book series; Endgame is the sixth and final novel.
findings.evidence: Malorie Blackman official site; Penguin Noughts & Crosses series page

findings.truth: ‘Blanker’ is the slur for a nought. ‘Dagger’ is used by noughts for a Cross.
findings.evidence: RSC 2007 Teacher Pack; Illuminate Publishing Noughts & Crosses Play Guide, Act 1 Scene 7 and Act 2 Scene 19

findings.claim: The knowledge check marks ‘dagger’ as the slur for a nought and does not offer ‘blanker’.
findings.truth: The correct answer is ‘blanker’; ‘dagger’ refers to a Cross.
findings.evidence: RSC 2007 Teacher Pack; Illuminate Publishing Noughts & Crosses Play Guide, Act 1 Scene 7 and Act 2 Scene 19

findings.claim: The play was later toured by Pilot Theatre, including productions in 2019 and 2022.
findings.truth: Pilot Theatre’s 2019 and 2022–23 productions used Sabrina Mahfouz’s separate adaptation, not Cooke’s prescribed version.
findings.evidence: Pilot Theatre Noughts & Crosses production page; spec 4.2 set-play list

findings.claim: This is what the spec means by subtext in performance.
findings.truth: The specification does not use or define ‘subtext’; the explanation is valid drama vocabulary but should not be attributed to the specification.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2.1.2 and full-text check of specs/aqa/drama-8261-8261.md

findings.claim: Kamal Hadley is equivalent to a Home Secretary.
findings.truth: Sources conflict: the RSC 2007 pack calls him a Home Office minister, while the RSC page and contemporary reviews describe Sephy as a Prime Minister’s or Deputy Prime Minister’s daughter. Use ‘senior Cross politician’ unless the prescribed edition resolves the role.
findings.evidence: RSC 2007 Information Pack; RSC Noughts & Crosses page; Guardian 2007 review
findings.ruling: Senior Cross politician; RSC office noted.

findings.claim: News bulletins and broadcast voiceovers are a non-diegetic device.
findings.truth: The documented RSC staging has characters turn on a television and then receive the report, which makes that use diegetic. Either revise all linked references to news reports as diegetic media or retain them only as optional sound-design choices; do not make a partial change.
findings.evidence: Daily Info review of the 2007 RSC production; affected content, practice, match and flashcard fields
findings.ruling: Diegetic vs non-diegetic news bulletins is a staging interpretation; the lesson's voiceover reading is a legitimate directorial choice. Left, recorded.

summary: Six verified findings have surgical edits. Two source-conflicted or multi-field issues are retained for adjudication.
